assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and its experimental realisation turned quantum information processing from a thought experiment into a laboratory discipline. Original, clear, and with enormous lasting impact on quantum computing and simulation.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive theoretical proposal; Blatt is the leading experimental realiser of the gate and of scalable ion-trap processors. Wineland (already recognised in 2012 for related ion control) and Monroe are not creditable here, so the experimental side is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many independent groups over about thirty years; the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely, with the field now commercially and scientifically prominent.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for ion manipulation could be read as partial prior recognition.
Whether Blatt or another experimentalist is the best third laureate is open within the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation is a cornerstone of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, defining a universality class for stochastic interface growth with exact connections to random matrices (Tracy-Widom statistics). It is conceptually clean, original, and has influenced mathematics and physics broadly. From my own work in stochastic processes and random matrices I regard this as unusually deep.
assessment.attribution: Kardar and Zhang are natural theory recipients (the original paper also had a third author not in the supplied credit, which complicates the allocation); Takeuchi provided the decisive experimental confirmation of the exponents and distributions in liquid-crystal turbulence.
assessment.maturity: Theory dates from 1986; exact solutions and the liquid-crystal experiments of 2010-2011 give strong independent confirmation. Recognition is mature, though experimental realisations beyond one platform are fewer.
uncertainties: The original KPZ paper has an additional author outside the supplied credited names, so a fair prize configuration is hard.
Breadth of experimental confirmation across systems is not fully verified by me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave the first controlled non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, capturing the Mott transition and enabling realistic materials calculations (DFT+DMFT). It is a fundamental conceptual and computational advance.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit, Georges and Kotliar the mapping to a quantum impurity problem; the supplied list lacks Metzner, so the configuration only partly reflects the full history of credit.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use, validation against experiment and extension to materials; very mature and stable.
uncertainties: Omission of Walter Metzner and Antoine Georges-Krauth/Rozenberg contributions from the supplied credit leaves attribution unresolved.
Quantitative reliability for some materials is still debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's implementation and extension, has pushed time measurement to the 10^-18 level and opened tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. A clear invention with demonstrated impact.
assessment.attribution: Two credited names map well onto proposal and demonstration. Others (Hall, Hänsch were recognised in 2005; ion-clock groups are separate) are outside this candidate, so the configuration is clean.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many laboratories and approaching a redefinition of the second; mature, perhaps slightly ahead of full redefinition.
uncertainties: Competition with ion-clock approaches may complicate the narrative of priority.
Practical impact (redefinition of the second) is still pending.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Vicsek model and the Toner-Tu hydrodynamic theory established that long-range order in two-dimensional flocks is possible, a striking departure from the Mermin-Wagner expectation, and founded the field of active matter. Original, clear, and broadly influential from biology to materials. This is close to my own research interests, so I try to hold it to the same standard as others.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek proposed the minimal model; Toner and Tu derived the continuum theory and the scaling predictions. These three are reasonable, though Ramaswamy and others made related contributions not in the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Theory is decades old; experiments on bird flocks, bacteria and colloids support aspects, but quantitative tests of the Toner-Tu exponents remain limited. Reasonably mature, somewhat less confirmed than the top candidates.
uncertainties: Quantitative experimental confirmation of the predicted exponents is incomplete.
Credit among Vicsek, Toner, Tu and others in the wider active-matter field may be disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting phases in twisted bilayer graphene opened the moire materials field, with a clear theory-experiment pair and large impact.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero led the experimental discovery. Co-authors on the experiments (Cao and others) are not credited, but the three-person configuration is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Broadly replicated across many groups but the origin of the superconductivity and correlated states remains actively debated, so the physics is not yet stable; perhaps slightly premature.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and nature of the correlated states are unresolved.
Junior experimental contributors are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics established strong light-matter coupling on a chip and is the architecture for most superconducting quantum processors. Clear and highly impactful.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues made the 2004 theoretical proposal and Wallraff and Schoelkopf the first experiments; Devoret, Martinis and Clarke were recognised by the 2025 prize for related circuit work, so the overlap affects the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Extremely well confirmed and widely reproduced; but the recent 2025 prize on superconducting circuits may make a quick follow-up less timely.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum effects in circuits.
Possible disagreement over whether Blais or others should share credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming phase diagram unified glasses, granular matter and foams through a common transition with critical scaling, a concept that organises disordered matter. Original and conceptually clear.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel proposed the unifying jamming picture; the supplied credit is compact and plausible, though O'Hern, Silbert, Durian and others made important contributions.
assessment.maturity: Simulations and experiments support the main picture, but the relation to the glass transition and the universality of exponents remain contested, so maturity is moderate.
uncertainties: Connection between jamming and the glass transition is not settled.
Credit to simulation co-authors is unaddressed in the supplied names.
